correctness.rationale: Axioms of a finite projective plane give connectedness, exact shore-specific distance-two clique patterns and no four-cycles. Every mixed simplex has at most one vertex from one shore. The two cover pieces collapse onto contractible pure-shore complexes; their intersection is exactly the edge-deleted incidence graph. Homotopy pushout gives suspension and q^3-t spheres. Natural Mayer-Vietoris maps equal graph cycle inclusions, and fundamental cycles built from a spanning tree prove the coordinate cokernels split over integers. A leaf domination supplies endpoint compatibility. Standard-library verifier exhaustively checks all q=2,3 intermediate stages, clique faces, collapses and mod-two Betti ranks; finite checks corroborate and do not substitute for the general proof.

value.rationale: A canonical one-point incidence-failure filtration interpolates from intact projective-plane Rips topology to previously studied vertex puncture across every finite projective plane, including non-Desarguesian ones. Exactly one primitive integral two-sphere is lost per edge, with complete split maps and no torsion; endpoint domination clarifies why q edge failures equal point removal. This is a motivated, all-order exact stability law, rather than an arbitrary finite parameter slice or a restatement of the known endpoints.
